title: Victorious in one person, overcome in another
source_text: LXIV. Porro quanquam victrix illa delectatio, in qua Christi gratia medicinalis & efficax consistit, voluntatem ad bonum, secundum illius doctrinam, impellat infallibiliter, & bono, quod ita suave est, certo consentire faciat: nihilominus quae in uno victrix est, quia minor ei se opponit carnis delectatio, quaeque idcirco voluntatem in consensum inducit, in alio tamen majori & fortiori carnis delectatione vincetur, nec per eam flectetur voluntas, quam captivam abducet delectatio terrena potentior atque valentior.
pass_a_gloss: LXIV. Further although that victorious delight, in which the medicinal and efficacious grace of Christ consists, according to his doctrine, impels the will to good infallibly, and makes it certainly consent to the good, which is thus sweet: nevertheless that which in one is victorious, because a lesser delight of the flesh opposes itself to it, and which therefore brings the will into consent, in another yet will be conquered by a greater and stronger delight of the flesh, nor will the will be bent through it, which a more powerful and stronger earthly delight will lead away captive.
pass_b_english: Thesis LXIV. Although, on his teaching, that victorious delight in which Christ's healing and efficacious grace consists drives the will to the good infallibly and makes it surely consent to the good that is so sweet, nevertheless a delight that wins in one person, because the delight of the flesh opposing it there is weaker, and so brings the will to consent, will in another person be overcome by a greater and stronger delight of the flesh. There it will not bend the will, which a mightier and stronger earthly delight will lead away captive.

lemmas.gloss: that which in one is victorious

lemmas.latin: quam captivam abducet delectatio terrena potentior atque valentior
lemmas.gloss: which a more powerful and stronger earthly delight will lead away captive

choices.why: Jansenius's term for Christ's grace as remedy for the fallen will; kept as in XLI.

bible_refs: Cornelius Jansenius, Augustinus (Louvain, 1640), tome 3, De gratia Christi Salvatoris, book 4, chapters 6-9.
